elements.name: washer thickness (thin, .032 in)
elements.note: 0.032 +/-0.004 in. This is the washer actually ballooned in DETAIL B (find 32, NAS1149V0332H) -- but the workbook never evaluated a check with it. See the worksheet.

source_ref.note: Part present on 217755 as NAS1149V0332H (find 32, qty 9), nomenclature '.203" X .438" X .032" MIN'. The parts list says .032 MIN; the workbook models it as .032 +/-.004. The NAS1149 standard is not in this repo, so the +/-.004 is untraced. DOWNGRADED `inferred` -> `untraced` 2026-08-10 (handoff fastener_citations_and_confidence): the note above already ended '+/-.004 is untraced' while the field said `inferred`, which is the note-vs-field defect one notch below the 2026-08-06 correction. Decided on the merits rather than relabelled to `parts_list`: the parts list corroborates that this washer exists in the joint and gives a MINIMUM, not a nominal with a band -- so it supports neither number the stack folds. The only support for .032 +/-.004 is 'the workbook says so', which the SOP makes `untraced` no matter how reasonable it looks. It is now on the gap list, where the SOP's one hard rule requires it. NAS1149 closes it.

elements.name: thread transition allowance (all fasteners)
elements.note: 1/16 in. Not a measured feature: the run-out length between full shank diameter and full thread. The workbook's 'nominal' is its MAXIMUM (min is 0), so nominal-column shank-out results are pessimistic by up to 0.79 mm.

source_ref.note: Rule-of-thumb allowance, no cited standard. CORRECTION 2026-08-06: the parenthetical that used to end this note -- 'that spec is not in this repo' -- went stale when NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4.pdf arrived in data/inbox/specs/. DECIDED 2026-08-10 (handoff fastener_citations_and_confidence), on the merits and with the value UNCHANGED: NAS6403 does not print this quantity, so the element stays `kind: assumed` / `untraced` and stays on the gap list. What sheet 1 actually gives, read off a crop: T (Ref) = .323 in for NAS6403, which is length minus grip (1.135 - .812 = .323 exactly, from the sheet-3 dash-13 row) -- i.e. the WHOLE region from the end of the full cylindrical shank to the point, thread and run-out and point chamfer together. The 1/16 in modelled here is the run-out INSIDE that region, and taking T for it would be an 8.2 mm allowance where the workbook assumed 1.6 mm. Sheet 2 note (b) additionally makes T a reference dimension, 'for design purposes only, not an inspection requirement'. The only other candidates on sheet 1 are ruled out by sheet 2's own notes: X (g) = .156 in is '5 thread pitches', the minimum female-thread engagement region for the MIL-F-18240 locking element, and Y (h) = .094 in is '3 thread pitches' in which the locking element must not be effective -- both measured in pitches from the threaded end (.156 = 5/32, .094 = 3/32 at the .1900-32 pitch of 1/32 in), neither a run-out length. So NAS6403 dimensions grip and length and gives their difference as a reference, and never dimensions the transition itself. The document that would close it is MIL-S-8879, the thread spec sheet 1 invokes for the UNJF-3A threads, and it is NOT in data/inbox/specs/ -- the same gap already recorded on hardware_entries.json's NAS6403U11D. This term is the single most pessimistic in the tan-link shank-out checks (its 'nominal' is its maximum, min is 0); leaving it alone leaves those check results where they were.

elements.name: fastener grip, -13 (.812 in)
elements.note: 0.812 +/-0.010 in. RE-CITED 2026-08-10 (handoff fastener_citations_and_confidence): the band now comes off the NAS6403 standard, not the parts list -- the same move fastener_grip_14 made on 2026-08-06.

source_ref.note: Both the .812 nominal and the ±.010 band are printed on sheet 3: the value in the 'Grip ±.010' column, the band in that column's own header ('LENGTH ±.015' heads the per-basic-number columns beside it). Sheet 2 CODE block decodes the part number -- 'Dash number indicates grip in .0625 increments' (13 x .0625 = .8125, printed .812), 'U' after the basic number = unplated, 'H' after the dash number = drilled HEAD (not shank: the -14 in this same joint is 'D', drilled shank) -- and sheet 2 note (a) defines grip: 'from the underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical portion of the shank'. WAS `kind: parts_list` / `confidence: inferred` citing 217755 find 95, whose own note admitted 'the grip +/-.010 comes from the workbook here, not from this citation'; a parts list gives the nomenclature nominal and never a band. Which bolt this is remains the parts list's evidence: NAS6403U13H, find 95, qty 3, and -- unlike the -14 -- ballooned on NO sheet of 217755, so the parts list is the only place it appears at all. The `source_ref.export` block that named the 2026-JUL-23 POST export of 217755 by sha256 was DROPPED with the parts-list citation, exactly as fastener_grip_14's was on 2026-08-06: it described a citation this element no longer makes, and `kind: "spec"` is exempt from the export requirement because data/inbox/specs/ is append-only, so the filename identifies the bytes (test_every_drawing_citation_says_which_export_it_was_read_from). That same export block is still live on this stack's straight_bushing if the sha256 is wanted. Scan, no text layer -- read by vision from a crop, command in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260810_fastener_citations_and_confidence.md.

source_ref.note: Both the .875 nominal and the ±.010 band are printed on sheet 3: the value in the 'Grip ±.010' column, the band in that column's own header. Sheet 2 CODE block decodes the part number -- 'Dash number indicates grip in .0625 increments' (14 x .0625 = .875), 'U' after the basic number = unplated, 'D' after the dash number = drilled shank -- and sheet 2 note (a) defines what grip means: 'from the underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical portion of the shank'.
